items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that the continuous random variable [MATH: Z] follows a standard normal distribution:

Content:
[MATH: Z\sim N(0,1)]

Content:
The standard normal distribution is symmetric about the vertical axis. We can use this fact to help us calculate probabilities.

Content:
For example, the two shaded areas below are equal.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/0cb4db7bd66551fad0b2f5b811e48d2a]

Content:
Note that

Content:
- the shaded area on the left corresponds to [MATH: P(Z \lt -a),] and
- the shaded area on the right corresponds to [MATH: P(Z \gt a).]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/750d46685f52f34c6ed909816f011a81]

Content:
Since these two areas are equal by symmetry, we have the following rule:

Content:
[MATH: P(Z \gt a) = P(Z \lt -a)]

Content:
Similarly, we have that

Content:
[MATH: P(Z \gt -a) = P(Z \lt a) = \Phi(a),]

Content:
as shown below. Recall that [MATH: \Phi(z)] is the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/896a96349cab4d47e25199d59ea3bcb8]

Content:
Let's take a look at some concrete examples.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
For a random variable [MATH: Z \sim N(0,1)] we have the following symmetry property for [MATH: a > 0{:}]

[MATH: P(Z \gt -a) = P(Z \lt a) = \Phi(a)]

We're given that [MATH: Z\sim N(0,1),] and we wish to compute [MATH: P( Z > -0.76).] The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability [MATH: P(Z \lt 0.76).]

Therefore,

[MATH: P(Z > -0.76) = P(Z < 0.76) = \Phi(0.76) = 0.7764.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
For a random variable [MATH: Z \sim N(0,1),] we have the following symmetry property for [MATH: a > 0{:}]

[MATH: P(Z \gt a) = P(Z \lt -a) = \Phi(-a)]

We're given that [MATH: Z\sim N(0,1),] and we wish to compute [MATH: P( Z \lt -1.54).] The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability [MATH: P(Z \gt 1.54).]

Therefore,

[MATH: P(Z < − 1.54)|= P(Z > 1.54); = 1 − P(Z < 1.54); = 1 − Φ(1.54); = 1 − 0.9382; = 0.0618.]

[MATH: P(− 0.53 < Z < 0.53)|= P(Z < 0.53) − P(Z ≤ − 0.53); = P(Z ≤ 0.53) − P(Z ≤ − 0.53); = Φ(0.53) − Φ(− 0.53)]

[MATH: P(− 0.53 < Z < 0.53)|= Φ(0.53) − Φ(− 0.53); = 0.7019 − 0.2981; = 0.4038.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose that the continuous random variable [MATH: Z] follows a standard normal distribution:

Content:
[MATH: Z\sim N(0,1)]

Content:
The standard normal distribution is symmetric about the vertical axis. We can use this fact to help us calculate probabilities.

Content:
For example, the two shaded areas below are equal.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/0cb4db7bd66551fad0b2f5b811e48d2a]

Content:
Note that

Content:
- the shaded area on the left corresponds to [MATH: P(Z \lt -a),] and
- the shaded area on the right corresponds to [MATH: P(Z \gt a).]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/750d46685f52f34c6ed909816f011a81]

Content:
Since these two areas are equal by symmetry, we have the following rule:

Content:
[MATH: P(Z \gt a) = P(Z \lt -a)]

Content:
Similarly, we have that

Content:
[MATH: P(Z \gt -a) = P(Z \lt a) = \Phi(a),]

Content:
as shown below. Recall that [MATH: \Phi(z)] is the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/896a96349cab4d47e25199d59ea3bcb8]

Content:
Let's take a look at some concrete examples.

---

Item 2 — Example: Computing a Probability on an Unbounded Interval

Example Prompt:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function [MATH: \Phi(z)] for the standard normal distribution. Given that [MATH: Z \sim N(0,1),] compute [MATH: P(Z \gt -0.76).]

| [MATH: z] | [MATH: \, 0.05 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.06 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.07 \,] |
| [MATH: \, 0.6 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.7422 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.7454 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.7486 \,] |
| [MATH: \, 0.7 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.7734 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.7764 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.7794 \,] |
| [MATH: \, 0.8 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.8023 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.8051 \,] | [MATH: \, 0.8078 \,] |

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
[IMG: /graphics/66fefa957dd168d1589cdb34bce3bced]

For a random variable [MATH: Z \sim N(0,1)] we have the following symmetry property for [MATH: a > 0{:}]

[MATH: P(Z \gt -a) = P(Z \lt a) = \Phi(a)]

We're given that [MATH: Z\sim N(0,1),] and we wish to compute [MATH: P( Z > -0.76).] The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

[IMG: /graphics/1bc0f3dd71234ca7671872a937519a38]

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability [MATH: P(Z \lt 0.76).]

[IMG: /graphics/bd8ed379c32619927570445941878c4f]

Therefore,

[MATH: P(Z > -0.76)
= P(Z < 0.76)
= \Phi(0.76)
= 0.7764.]
